background: M.S. in Learning, Design and Technology at Stanford GSE (in progress); M.A. in Applied Linguistics (Distinction), UCL; four years teaching English (high school and college) in China, where I used AI-assisted essay scoring and saw AI widen gaps between students. Built Knowledge Echoes, a teacher-in-the-loop dashboard that highlights growth across students' writing. At Stanford: Math Out Loud with Prof. Dora Demszky, coding how multilingual elementary students engage with peers' mathematical ideas across 415 classroom observations and comparing human vs LLM coding (78% of coder disagreements were about referencing vs extending a peer's idea); building a platform with Dr. Karin Forssell (feedback-paths.vercel.app) that tracks how second-language writers accept, question, adapt or reject AI feedback and how they revise; AI Tinkery mentor with Gregory Wilson. Interests: human–human and human–AI interaction in learning, collaborative learning analytics, AI feedback and writing, epistemic agency, equitable participation, teacher-facing analytics.

keyFacts.text: NYU Steinhardt allows only ONE application per term. Choose one program (ECT, Teaching & Learning, or Applied Linguistics).
TC allows only one active application per cycle. Choose between the PhD in Technology, Media and Learning and the EdD in Applied Linguistics. For Waring, pick the "language use" track.
Penn GSE virtual doctoral open house Tue Nov 17, 7:30pm ET (4:30pm PT), with Literacy Studies and Learning Sciences breakout rooms. Amy Stornaiuolo recommends it.
Penn: Bodong Chen admits only through LST. Literacy Studies admits 1-2 per year; Amy suggests also naming Gerald Campano. Two Penn applications need different recommenders.

NYU's English-test exemption needs 4 years of US/English-only study, so your Stanford MS and UCL MA likely don't exempt you. Plan to send TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo (successful applicants typically score ~100 iBT). TC, Penn and CUNY appear to accept your UCL MA as an exemption. Verify.
Lehigh TLT: Dec 1 is the spring-start deadline and Apr 1 is for fall, but you must apply by Dec 1 to be considered for funding. Keep Dec 1.
Confirm your Rutgers specialization: your email to Dr. Abas says Literacy Education, but your program list says LCID / Learning Sciences.
Sarah Beck doesn't expect to take a student this cycle (Teaching & Learning).
